title: AI-Powered Email Threat Detection, GeoLocation and Forensic Intelligence Platform
org: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE)
description:
• Background Email continues to be one of the most widely used communication channels in government, education, banking,and enterprise ecosystems. However, it also remains one of the most exploited attack vectors for phishing,impersonation, business email compromise, financial fraud, credential theft, and malware delivery. Threat actors increasingly use spoofed domains, deceptive sender identities, social engineering techniques, and compromised infrastructure to send highly convincing fraudulent emails that appear legitimate to end users.Traditional email security controls such as spam filters, static blacklists, and rule-based signature mechanisms are often insufficient to detect sophisticated fraudulent emails. Attackers now use AI-generated language,domain lookalikes, display-name spoofing, hidden redirection links, and relay chains to evade standard detection systems. In many cases, even when a suspicious email is identified, organizations lack the technical capability to effectively trace the source path, identify probable sender infrastructure, correlate geolocation clues, and support investigation into the origin of the email.This gap creates major challenges for cybersecurity teams, law enforcement support, fraud response units, and institutional administrators who need not only to detect malicious emails but also to investigate their source and reveal indicators that may help identify the actor or infrastructure behind the attack.
• Problem Statement Current email security ecosystems primarily focus on filtering or blocking suspicious content but provide limited intelligence for deep forensic tracing of fraudulent email origins. Existing tools often do not adequately correlate email headers, SMTP relay paths, SPF/DKIM/DMARC validation results, IP reputation, geolocation indicators, domain registration intelligence, and behavioral patterns to build a complete picture of the sender’s identity or operating location.There is a need for an AI-powered platform capable of detecting phishing, spoofed, impersonated, and fraudulent emails in real time or near real time, analyzing the complete technical structure of an email, tracing its transmission path across mail servers, estimating its origin with location, and generating forensic intelligence and investigative insights that assist in identifying malicious infrastructure, compromised systems, or threat actors behind the attack.The solution should support forensic analysis, fraud prevention, institutional email security, and investigation workflows while maintaining legal, privacy, and evidentiary standards.
• Proposed Solution Develop an AI-Powered Email Threat Detection, GeoLocation and Forensic Intelligence Platform that combines Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML), email header forensics, IP intelligence, domain analysis, and graph-based correlation to identify suspicious emails,detect advanced email threats, and investigate their probable origin.
The system should ingest raw email content, metadata, and headers; validate sender authentication mechanisms;
extract indicators of compromise; reconstruct relay paths; analyze originating IP addresses and associated geolocation data; and generate a confidence-based assessment of fraud risk and probable sender origin. The platform should provide actionable alerts, visual trace maps, and forensic reports for security analysts,administrators, and investigators.
• Key Components
• Fraudulent Email Detection Engine o NLP-based analysis of email subject lines, body text, urgency cues, impersonation language, and social engineering patterns.
o Detection of phishing indicators such as spoofed sender addresses, deceptive domains, suspicious attachments, malicious links, and obfuscated URLs.
o AI/ML models to classify emails as legitimate, suspicious, impersonated, phishing, or fraud-related.
o Identification of business email compromise patterns such as payment diversion, fake invoice requests, credential harvesting attempts, and executive impersonation.
• Email Header and Protocol Analysis Module o Deep analysis of email headers including Return-Path, Received headers, Message-ID, Reply-To,DKIM signatures, SPF alignment, and DMARC status.
o Detection of anomalies in mail routing, forged sender fields, relay manipulation, and spoofed transmission records.
o Validation of whether the email was sent through authorized infrastructure or suspicious relay paths.
• Origin Traceability and Location Analysis o Extraction of originating IP addresses from header chains and identification of the earliest reliable sending node.
o IP geolocation mapping to estimate the likely country, region, city, ISP, hosting provider, or proxy service associated with the email source.
o Correlation with VPN, TOR, open relay, botnet, or cloud-hosted infrastructure indicators where applicable.
o Domain intelligence analysis using WHOIS data, DNS records, MX records, hosting fingerprints,and registrar details to identify suspicious sender infrastructure.
• Identity Correlation and Attribution Support o Correlation of email indicators with known threat intelligence, blacklists, previous incidents,domain clusters, and repeated fraud campaigns.
o Graph-based relationship analysis between sender domains, IP addresses, aliases, reply chains, and linked infrastructure.
o Confidence-based investigative assessment to assist in revealing probable sender identity, associated infrastructure, or campaign-level attribution patterns.
o Support for flagging whether the email likely originated from a compromised account, spoofed domain, anonymized infrastructure, or direct malicious actor environment.
• Alerting, Dashboard, and Forensic Reporting o Real-time alerts for high-risk emails before user interaction or administrative approval.
o Analyst dashboard showing fraud score, spoofing indicators, sender trace path, geolocation map,and attribution confidence.
o Generation of structured forensic reports for institutional action, legal review, cyber incident response, and support to law enforcement agencies.
o Searchable case management view for grouping related fraudulent emails into campaigns.
• Privacy, Legal, and Compliance Safeguards o Controlled handling of personal data and metadata in accordance with organizational privacy policies.
o Logging, evidence preservation, and chain-of-custody support for investigation purposes.
oConfigurable retention and masking mechanisms for sensitive communication data.
• Expected Outcomes
• Early and accurate detection of fraudulent, spoofed, and phishing-based email attacks.
• Improved ability to trace suspicious email origin paths and identify probable source infrastructure.
• Enhanced fraud investigation capability through geolocation analysis, domain intelligence, and sender attribution support.
• Reduced financial loss, reputational damage, and unauthorized disclosure of confidential information caused by email-based fraud.
• Better institutional readiness for cyber incident response, forensic investigation, and enforcement coordination.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, ml, machine learning applied to a blockchain & cybersecurity problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Blockchain & Cybersecurity. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on real-time, protocol, infrastructure. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 21/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: AI-Powered Email Threat Detection, GeoLocation and Forensic Intelligence Platform

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that not only detects sophisticated phishing and business email compromise, but traces where the email actually came from, tracking relay chains and infrastructure clues, giving investigators forensic evidence instead of just a spam-filter block.
overview.why_it_matters: Modern attackers use AI-generated language and domain lookalikes that beat traditional filters. Beyond just blocking, genuine forensic tracing gives organizations the ability to actually investigate and respond to sophisticated attacks.
pain_points: Traditional email security (spam filters, blacklists, signatures) can't catch sophisticated AI-generated phishing.
Attackers use domain lookalikes, spoofing, and relay chains to evade detection.
Organizations lack technical capability to trace email origin and support investigation.
overview.background: Email remains a top attack vector, and traditional security controls are increasingly insufficient against AI-generated, sophisticated phishing that also evades post-incident forensic tracing.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI-powered platform detecting sophisticated email threats (phishing, BEC, spoofing) and providing forensic intelligence including geolocation clues and sender-infrastructure tracing.
expected_solution: AI-based detection of sophisticated/AI-generated phishing content.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Combines content-based AI phishing detection with genuine forensic header/metadata analysis and geolocation correlation, real technical breadth beyond a standard spam filter.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Requires both NLP-based phishing content detection and real email-header forensic analysis (SPF/DKIM/DMARC, relay tracing), substantial cross-domain depth.

competitive_landscape.note: Genuine email-security forensics is a specialized niche, requires both ML and email-protocol/security domain knowledge together.

innovation.note: Combines AI content detection with genuine forensic header analysis and geolocation, beyond standard spam-filter functionality.

invention.note: Requires both NLP phishing-detection modeling and real email-protocol forensic analysis together.

technical_feasibility.note: Public phishing email datasets and email header/protocol standards (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) are well-documented and directly usable.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly addresses a top, real-world attack vector with genuine investigative/forensic value.

architecture.note: Content analysis plus header/metadata forensic analysis feeding a unified reporting output, well-understood pattern.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, genuinely achievable with real public data. The forensic tracing half is the harder, more differentiating component worth investing real time in, not just a content-based spam classifier.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Public phishing datasets and well-documented email authentication standards (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) give real, accessible technical grounding.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building only content-based phishing detection without genuine header/forensic analysis would miss the PS's explicitly-named differentiator, tracing origin and supporting investigation.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Invest real build time in the forensic header-analysis component specifically (SPF/DKIM/DMARC verification, relay-chain reconstruction from Received headers), not just a text-based phishing classifier.

idea_0_4: Source public phishing email datasets and research email authentication standards (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and header structure.
Design your two-part architecture: content-based AI phishing detection plus header-based forensic analysis.
Split: one person on the content/NLP detection, one on the header/forensic analysis.
prototype_4_22: Build your AI-based phishing content classifier.
Build your header-parsing and forensic analysis (SPF/DKIM/DMARC verification, Received-header relay-chain reconstruction).
Start correlating header IP information with geolocation data.
integration_22_30: Connect content detection and forensic analysis into one unified threat report.
Test against a mix of genuine phishing samples and legitimate emails to confirm accurate discrimination.
Build the forensic report output, relay chain, geolocation clues, authentication failures.
polish_30_36: Polish the forensic report presentation for genuine investigator usability.
Rehearse a live demo analyzing a real (or realistic sample) phishing email, showing both content flagging and forensic trace.
Prepare to discuss the limits of geolocation from header data (proxies, VPNs can obscure true origin).
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your forensic analysis correctly reconstructing a relay chain and flagging authentication failures on a real phishing sample, that trace-and-investigate capability is the genuine differentiator beyond standard spam filtering.

strengths: Public data and well-documented email standards give real, accessible technical grounding.
Genuine forensic/investigative capability differentiates from standard spam filtering.
weaknesses: Geolocation from email headers has real limitations (proxies, VPNs, spoofed headers), must be presented honestly.
Requires both ML and email-protocol domain expertise together.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Don't skip the forensics/protocol role, that's the genuine differentiator over standard content-based spam filtering.
team_fit.approach: Research email authentication protocols (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) and header structure thoroughly, this technical grounding is essential for the forensic half.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The content-based phishing classifier using standard NLP techniques.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Correctly parsing and interpreting email headers for genuine forensic value (relay chains, authentication status), that requires real email-protocol domain knowledge.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A system that only does content-based classification without genuine forensic header analysis would just be a relabeled spam filter, missing the PS's actual differentiating ask.

data_resource_availability.status: Public phishing email datasets and email authentication standards are genuinely accessible for real training and testing.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not needed, real data access is achievable here.

judge_qna.question: How accurate is your geolocation tracing, given that attackers often use VPNs or proxies to obscure origin?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be honest about this real limitation, describe what your geolocation actually reflects (likely relay/proxy location, not necessarily true attacker origin) and how you present that uncertainty rather than false certainty.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would an investigator actually use imperfect geolocation data in a real investigation?

judge_qna.question: How does your system handle a sophisticated, AI-generated phishing email that passes traditional authentication checks (SPF/DKIM valid because sent from a compromised legitimate account)?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Address this directly, content-based AI detection is exactly what catches this case since header authentication alone wouldn't flag it, describe how your two components complement each other for this scenario.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your detection rate specifically for compromised-account-based attacks versus spoofed-domain attacks?
